CorrectiveAction.name: Repair or replace damaged tool part
CorrectiveAction.description: Properly repair or replace the damaged part of a tool.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Check for damaged parts and tools before operating the machine. 2. Any damaged part of a tool should be properly repaired or replaced. 3. Do not operate the machine if any component does not appear to be functioning correctly.

CorrectiveAction.name: Replace damaged window panel
CorrectiveAction.description: Replace the damaged or severely scratched window immediately.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Replace windows immediately if they are damaged or severely scratched. 2. Contact the factory for replacement panels.

CorrectiveAction.name: Turn off power for excessive ambient temperature
CorrectiveAction.description: Turn off power immediately when ambient temperature exceeds the limit.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Immediately turn off power if ambient temperature exceeds 105 degrees Fahrenheit (40 degrees C).

CorrectiveAction.name: Reset machine home position after absolute encoder loss
CorrectiveAction.description: Press-offset setting-parameter-write enable (OFS/SET hard key twice) set parameter bit to a 1; the “key” needs to be switched to the [0] position, the key cannot be removed, and this enables the write capability.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Press-offset setting-parameter-write enable (OFS/SET hard key twice) set parameter bit to a 1. The “key” needs to be switched to the [0] position, the key cannot be removed, this enables the write capability. 2. Press system (hard key)- type 1815 -press -no. Search (this will find parameter 1815 which is the reference position parameter setting- set APZ bits for axis wishing to reference to 0. If you already have an alarm about lost encoder position the troubled axis will have a zero set in this bit, you can go to step 4. 3. Power down completely. 4. Power up, drives on and jog the axis requiring referencing to align with scribe marks on red painted washer. Be very careful you do not crash the machine! 5. Change 1815 APZ bit to 1 for axis wishing to reference. Change the parameter write enable bit to 0. 5. Power down completely. 6. Power up, drives on, the axis display should read 0 and there should be no alarms.

CorrectiveAction.name: Adjust backlash compensation
CorrectiveAction.description: Adjust backlash compensation according to the procedure outlined below in Section 3.33.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Adjust backlash compensation according to the procedure outlined below in Section 3.33.

CorrectiveAction.name: Adjust ballscrew endplay
CorrectiveAction.description: Adjust ballscrew endplay when it is greater than 0.0001".
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Loosen the 3 set screws on the ballscrew spanner nut adjacent to the motor coupling. 2. Using a spanner wrench, tighten the nut. 3. Hold the ballscrew stationary with an allen key on the opposite end. 4. Tighten the set screws. 5. Recheck the endplay. 6. Repeat the tightening procedure if necessary. 7. Once the ballscrew endplay is .0001” or less, re-install any sheet metal or motor covers and re-install the waycover(s) as applicable.

CorrectiveAction.name: Align and reinstall waycover
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Slide the cover on the appropriate way surface, making sure that it is clear of debris. 2. Insert the cap head screws to the moving axis and the standoffs (if applicable), and hand-tighten only. 3. To properly align the waycover, jog the axis to the position where the waycover is in full extension, and then full compression. 4. With the waycover fully compressed, all cap head screws can now be tightened. 5. Run the axis back and forth slowly over full travel and check for any visual signs of misalignment. 6. Now rapid the axis back and forth over full travel again and check for any signs of misalignment.

CorrectiveAction.name: Clear alarm
CorrectiveAction.description: Clear an alarm from the control.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Press RESET. 2. Certain alarms will require a reboot of the control to clear.

CorrectiveAction.name: Correct carousel motor phasing
CorrectiveAction.description: Correct carousel rotation direction by changing incoming power phasing.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Switch any two incoming power wires at the disconnect. 2. Make sure the main power breaker is off.

CorrectiveAction.name: Recover from tool stuck in spindle after low air alarm
CorrectiveAction.description: Return the arm to its normal resting position after a tool change failure where the arm did not complete grabbing the tool.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Look to see what function did not complete. 2. Look at the solenoid valves; the solenoid valve that is illuminated is the operation that failed. 3. Press emergency stop. 4. If the arm did not complete grabbing the tool, make sure the pot is down and then press the arm return manual button. 5. After the arm is returned to normal resting position, tool is removed from the spindle and carousel pot returned manually, the carousel pots may have to be reset.

CorrectiveAction.name: Reset tool changer with manual solenoid overrides
CorrectiveAction.description: Operate the tool changer solenoid valves manually to reset the tool changer.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Access the air solenoid valves for the tool changer behind the door on the front of the ATC. 2. Run the solenoids manually by depressing the blue manual override buttons. 3. Push the buttons in sequence.

CorrectiveAction.name: Adjust Z axis height for smooth arm engagement
CorrectiveAction.description: Further adjust Z axis height when the arm does not respond smoothly.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Orient the spindle with an M19 command. 2. Install a tool in the spindle. 3. Press the middle right solenoid manual button to grab the tool. 4. Using the hand wheel at its finest setting or jog .001” increments move the Z axis, so the v flange groove of the tool is in the center of the arm v notch. 5. Record the machine coordinate value and retain for entry into parameter MC_1130. 6. Press the middle left solenoid manual button to remove the arm from the tool in the spindle. 7. Alternate the middle left and middle right button to check for smooth engagement of the arm into and away from the tool. 8. Remove tool from spindle. 9. Update parameter MC_1130 (Fanuc parameter P1241) with the new tool change height.

CorrectiveAction.name: Reset tool bin locations
CorrectiveAction.description: Reset all tool bin locations and bin table assignments.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. Remove tool from spindle. 2. In MDI command: M6T0 cycle start. 3. Remove any tool from spindle. 4. In MDI command: M61 cycle start (this will index carousel to bin #1). 5. Go to tool table, soft key F9, and then press soft key F9 bintbl, then F8 rstbins. 6. Fanuc, press system hard key, PMC soft key and params soft key, data soft key, and then dtble soft key, the data table bins 0 thru 24 will have to be edited to agree with the proper tool numbers. 7. Remove all tools from carousel and reinstall.

CorrectiveAction.name: Adjust spindle orient position
CorrectiveAction.description: Adjust the spindle orient position so the spindle keys align with the notch in the arm.
CorrectiveAction.instruction_text: 1. With Z axis at maximum positive limit and ATC arm under spindle nose (manual solenoid button 2nd on right), make sure spindle can be spun without spindle keys hitting ATC arm. 2. Orient spindle with M19A#degrees, start with #degrees=0 (example: M19A0). Fanuc will only accept M19. 3. Look to see if spindle keys are in alignment with notch in the arm. Command M5 cycle start. This will turn off the orient command. Fanuc machines you will have to change the orient position parameter P4031. 4. Repeat steps 2 and 3 and adjust “A” angle until correct (Fanuc machines change P4031). 5. Put this angle into parameter MC_5003.
